answer: A Sybil defense is a per-identity bond scaling with how many identities one operator runs, so each agent must lock stake plus a costly attestation. Splitting into N identities multiplies capital at risk instead of spreading it, and influence is weighted by bonded value minus slashing, so clones count less than one honest member. A reef shows the economics: many organisms attach, but each must secrete limestone, and prising one loose costs more than the shelter is worth. Clones leave a detectable pigment of timing and funding flows that validators slash; an idle clone ends as empty as a zephyr.
